title: split invoice line allocation and export fix for mid-cycle plan changes
creator: Sofia Alvarez
description: Summary: Customers who change subscription plans mid-billing-cycle (upgrade/downgrade or add seats) are seeing mismatched proration lines between Stripe invoices and our NetSuite exports. Symptoms include duplicate credit lines, missing prorated charges, and mismatched totals that fail NetSuite import validation. Root cause appears to be inconsistent line-splitting and rounding logic between the Stripe invoice_line_item model and our export aggregation step, combined with non-idempotent export row generation when retry logic triggers duplicates.
impact_details: Affected customers: ~0.6% of invoices in the last 30 days; errors surface as NetSuite import failures for some large accounts and as invoice total mismatches reported by Billing Ops. Downstream: revenue recognition delays and manual adjustments by finance. Risk: high for mid-month churn and seat-change heavy accounts.
acceptance_criteria: NetSuite export rows for invoices with mid-cycle plan changes exactly match Stripe line item totals after our transformation layer (no >$0.01 discrepancy)
Export job is idempotent: re-running the same invoice export produces no duplicate rows in the NetSuite CSV or export store
Automated end-to-end test added: sample invoices with multiple proration segments validate at export-time and after NetSuite import simulation
Monitoring: new dashboard tile surfaces proration mismatch rate and duplicate-export counts; alerts when mismatch rate > 0.1% over 24h
implementation_notes: Replace current aggregation step that sums prorated amounts using float summation with a strict decimal-based allocator that mirrors Stripe's split algorithm (use cents and integer math where possible)
Introduce canonical 'proration_segment_id' for each invoice line generated from a mid-cycle change and include it in export row keys to enforce idempotency
On retries, include original Stripe invoice.id + proration_segment_id hash to dedupe export rows before persistence
Add reconciliation job that compares exported NetSuite CSV totals against Stripe invoice totals nightly and emits a CSV of mismatches for finance
Add integration test harness that replays real failing invoices from the past 60 days through the new pipeline (anonymized)
steps_to_reproduce: Create a subscription and generate a full-cycle invoice in Stripe
Mid-cycle, change plan or seat count to cause Stripe to create multiple prorated invoice items
Trigger our billing export for the invoice and inspect the generated NetSuite CSV rows for that invoice id
Observe rounding differences (Stripe shows cents-sum that differs from our exported cents by > $0.01) and potential duplicate rows when export retries ran
Run NetSuite import validation against the CSV to reproduce failure cases
updates: 2025-10-22 - Sofia A.: Initial triage completed. Collected 42 failing invoices from last 30 days. Repro scripts and anonymized payloads uploaded to the billing-replay bucket.
2025-10-24 - Liam O.: Spike implemented: integer-cent allocator mirrors Stripe algorithm for basic two-segment proration. Unit tests added. Initial tests reduce mismatch count by ~78% on sampled set.

2025-10-28 - Finance (Monica R.): Confirmed sample NetSuite import passes when CSV matches Stripe totals exactly. Requested explicit audit columns (stripe_invoice_id, proration_segment_id) in export for tracing.

2025-10-30 - Liam O.: Added proration_segment_id and dedupe key to export schema. Integration tests show dedupe prevents duplicate rows on retry. Edge-case discovered: multi-currency invoices require base-currency normalization step.

2025-11-02 - Sofia A.: Plan: finish multi-currency normalization and run end-to-end replay on 60 anonymized invoices next week. Coordinate release with finance to run manual NetSuite dry-run on 2025-11-14 (low-traffic window).
rollback_plan: If export change causes unexpected NetSuite failures, revert to previous export binary, mark exports for manual reconciliation, and temporarily run nightly reconciliation job that produces adjustment entries for Finance. Post-mortem within 48h. Notify affected customers via Billing Ops if any invoices must be corrected.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: change impacts NetSuite mapping and revenue recognition exports. Mitigation: feature-flag the new allocator, run A/B export for non-production NetSuite instance first, and keep prior export format available. Finance sign-off required on CSV diff before full flip.
qa_plan: Unit tests for allocator and dedupe logic, integration replay of 60 anonymized invoices, NetSuite dry-run import by Finance, and staged rollout behind feature flag for 72h with tight monitoring. Post-release: run reconciliation job for 7 days and auto-open tickets for any mismatches.
owner_notes: Coordinate with Finance (Monica R.), Billing Ops (Jared K.), and SRE for rollout. PRs should include CSV diff artifacts and replay logs. Priority because manual adjustments are scaling up for month-end.
estimated_effort_notes: 8 points: 3 for allocator and idempotency changes, 2 for multi-currency normalization, 2 for tests and replay harness, 1 for dashboards/alerts
